messages.subject: Is GGIR for Preschoolers?
parts:
Hi there, 

I am a new GGIR user. I use wrist-worn actigraph GT9X to measure both preschoolers and parents' physical activity levels. I looked over all the publications that used GGIR, but failed to find anyone used this method to analyze preschoolers PA. I was wondering whether GGIR can be used for preschoolers? In addition, the shell function part 2 and part 5 need to define PA threshold (i.e., lig, mod, vig). So I also wonder whether these thresholds are different between adults and preschool children? 

I hope someone can lend your wisdom and advice a bit on these questions. Thank you very much for your time.

Best regards, 
Nan

messages.author: fe461312361bc741
messages.subject: Re: Is GGIR for Preschoolers?
parts:
Hi Nan,

GGIR can certainly be used in this case, but I am not aware of any specific thresholds with regards to your target group. I personally think, thresholds should not be adapted to every sample unless a lack of sensitivity does not allow to keep the existing ones. This will increase the comparability across different studies and at this stage the thresholds are somewhat arbitrary anyway. The default options worked well for my data. However, some details strongly depend on your research question (for example, would you like to differentiate between long and short bouts). The manual will help you there. I recommend preprocessing your data and comparing the results of different options in order to make an informed decision.

Regards,
David
